stories.headline: FT: Nvidia tells cloud clients at least 51% of their compute must go to non-Chinese customers

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has told cloud computing clients they must sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies, according to the Financial Times, citing five people familiar with the matter; no such restriction existed before.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker now requires cloud computing clients to sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies, the FT reported. The company previously had no such restrictions in place.

key_facts.fact: The instruction was delivered verbally through Nvidia's sales force and regional teams rather than in writing, applies to clients globally (not just Asia), and covers only future contracts, not existing leases.
key_facts.excerpt: The instructions were passed on verbally by Nvidia's sales and regional teams rather than put in writing. The rule applies to Nvidia's clients globally, not just those in Asia... It covers only future contracts, so existing leasing agreements stay as they are.

key_facts.fact: A rack of Nvidia B300 chips that sells for about $600,000 internationally traded in China last month for 18.5 million yuan (about $2.8 million) because of scarcity.
key_facts.excerpt: A rack of Nvidia B300 chips that sells for about $600,000 on the international market traded in China last month at 18.5 million yuan, or $2.8 million, because of scarcity.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia had already cut the number of Asian customers approved to buy its AI chips by more than half this year after drawing up a whitelist of companies that passed tightened compliance reviews.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia had already cut the number of Asian customers approved to buy its AI chips by more than half after drawing up a whitelist this year of companies that passed tightened compliance reviews.

key_facts.fact: A Singapore-based cloud provider said it is hard to find enough non-Chinese customers outside the US and that strict enforcement would hurt its business.
key_facts.excerpt: One Singapore-based group told FT it is hard to find enough non-Chinese customers outside the US, and that strict enforcement would hurt business.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report to AFP, saying data centers and clouds built on American chips are the foundation American model and application makers need to compete worldwide; China's foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she was not aware of the report.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report to AFP, but said in a statement that "datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide." ... Mao Ning said she was not aware of it.

stories.headline: Smugglers move Samsung and SK Hynix HBM into China via a loophole; Huawei's 960DT leans on it

key_facts.fact: Smugglers package export-controlled HBM from Samsung and SK Hynix on boards with cheap low-end server processors, because US export rules assess a package's computing power by the processor, not the memory, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: They are then paired with expensive HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, that, on their own, are banned for export to China. But because export control rules only look at the performance of the server processor and not at the other components attached to it, this allows the HBM chips attached inside them to slip under the radar.

key_facts.fact: In Shenzhen workshops, technicians heat the boards to melt the solder, lift off the memory stacks and discard the processors; the failure rate is high.
key_facts.excerpt: Local technicians apply heat to the board to melt the solder, detach only the necessary HBM, and discard the remaining server processors... the failure rate is high because applying heat too quickly or for an extended period can cause the memory stack to warp or crack.

key_facts.fact: A Chinese broker said one HBM3E unit now sells for about $4,000 in China, up from several hundred dollars a year ago; with 6 to 8 stacks per AI chip, memory alone costs $24,000 to $32,000.
key_facts.excerpt: the price of a single HBM3E, which traded for several hundred dollars just a year ago, has recently soared to about $4,000. A single AI chip package requires 6 to 8 HBMs. The memory price alone amounts to $24,000 to $32,000.

key_facts.fact: Huawei told some customers its next flagship AI chip, the Ascend 960DT, will largely use Samsung and SK Hynix HBM, and advised some customers to source the memory themselves.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies, whose next-generation Ascend 960DT AI accelerator is expected to rely heavily on HBM from Samsung Electronics and SK hynix... the company has reportedly asked some AI chip customers to source the memory themselves.

key_facts.fact: The Ascend 960DT is expected in Q1 2027 with double the memory bandwidth and capacity of Huawei's current chip; CXMT's HBM3E yields are reportedly just 20%-30%, versus about 70% at SK Hynix.
key_facts.excerpt: Expected in the first quarter of 2027, the Ascend 960DT is set to double the memory bandwidth and capacity of Huawei's current AI processor... CXMT's HBM3E yields remain at just 20%–30%, well below the approximately 70% achieved by South Korea's SK hynix.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said it strictly complies with US and Korean export controls and has not supplied Huawei since US restrictions began in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix stated, "We are strictly complying with relevant laws and regulations, including the export control regulations of the U.S. and South Korea," adding that it has never supplied products to Huawei since the implementation of U.S. export regulations in 2020.

stories.headline: Samsung to make HBM base dies for AMD and Nvidia at its second Taylor, Texas fab, report says

key_facts.fact: Samsung will use its second foundry plant in Taylor, Texas to produce HBM base dies for AMD and Nvidia, Maeil Business Newspaper reported on Nov. 3, citing industry sources; Samsung declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics will use its second foundry plant in Taylor, Texas, to produce base dies for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips for AMD and Nvidia... Samsung Electronics declined to comment on the matter.

key_facts.fact: Construction is due to formally start this month, the plant has secured orders for its entire output (mostly for AMD), and it will use 2nm technology across about 2.7 million square feet, roughly 1.5 times the first Taylor fab, which has a Tesla contract.
key_facts.excerpt: Construction is due to start formally this month, with the plant having secured orders for its entire output, and most of the secured volume is for AMD... The plant will use advanced 2-nanometre technology and cover about 2.7 million square feet, roughly 1.5 times the size of the first facility, which has a contract with Tesla.

key_facts.fact: Equipment installation is expected from February 2029, with mass production in 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Equipment is expected to be installed from February 2029, with mass production in 2030, Maeil said.

key_facts.fact: Base dies made in Taylor would be combined with DRAM core dies from Korea, and Broadcom, which makes AI chips for Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, could also be a customer, according to Maeil.
key_facts.excerpt: Once base dies are mass-produced there, they are expected to be combined with DRAM core dies made in Korea... base dies made at the Taylor fab could be supplied to Broadcom, which makes AI chips for Google, OpenAI and Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: A risk for Samsung: under Nvidia's proposed NVHBM standard, expected for HBM4E, TSMC would make all base dies, a design Nvidia says can raise memory bandwidth 30% and cut HBM power 15%.
key_facts.excerpt: A plan is underway for TSMC to manufacture all the base dies for NVHBM, a new HBM standard NVIDIA is promoting... It can increase memory bandwidth by 30%, reduce HBM power consumption by 15% and free up 25% more GPU area.

stories.headline: Churchill Capital XI holders approve $2.5B Agility Robotics SPAC; trading as AGLT set for Nov. 5

key_facts.fact: More than 84% of votes cast at Churchill Capital Corp XI's special shareholder meeting on Nov. 2 approved its merger with humanoid-robot maker Agility Robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 84% of votes cast at a special shareholder meeting on Nov. 2 supported the deal.

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close on Nov. 4, with the combined company trading on Nasdaq from Nov. 5 under the ticker AGLT; Churchill stock closed up nearly 14% on Nov. 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The SPAC is expected to close on Nov. 4. The combined company is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 5 under the ticker symbol AGLT. Churchill Capital stock finished up nearly 14% on Nov. 2.

key_facts.fact: The transaction gives Agility about $465 million in gross capital and values it at $2.5 billion pre-money; existing shareholders roll their equity over.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction is expected to provide Agility with approximately $465 million in gross capital before expenses... The original transaction valued Agility at a $2.5 billion pre-money equity value.

key_facts.fact: Digit robots operate in 9 customer environments, including GXO facilities, and Agility claims more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5, with general availability targeted for end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Its Digit robots are already operating in 9 customer environments... Agility has previously claimed it has more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5... general availability targeted for the end of that year.

sources.title: Churchill Capital XI shareholders approve $2.5B Agility Robotics humanoid SPAC

stories.headline: Warehouse-robot maker Tutor Intelligence raises $75M Series B led by a16z

key_facts.fact: Tutor Intelligence raised a $75 million Series B led by a16z, with participation from USV and Neo, its CEO Josh Gruenstein announced on Nov. 2.
key_facts.excerpt: We raised a $75M Series B to deploy intelligent robots now, led by @a16z, with participation from @usv and @neo.

key_facts.fact: The round brings Tutor's total funding to $117 million; its robots perform picking, towing and stacking, guided by remote human operators whose work feeds foundation models for the whole fleet.
key_facts.excerpt: Tutor Intelligence has secured $75 million in a Series B funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz, raising its total capital to $117 million... These robots utilize human input from remote operators to complete tasks, and every completed task generates data that updates foundation models for the entire fleet.

key_facts.fact: Tutor operates at almost 4x as many sites as a year ago and expects more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: We're in almost 4x as many sites as a year ago; nearly a third of this year's deployments went to existing customers coming back for more; and we're on track to have more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The money will go to frontier model training, robot manufacturing and deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: This round accelerates frontier model training, robot manufacturing, and deployment into industry.

stories.headline: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant plan a GW-scale AI data center at Drax Power Station, up to £20B

key_facts.fact: Drax signed an agreement with Brookfield and its UK AI-infrastructure platform Radiant to develop, deliver and operate an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire, targeting more than 1GW.
key_facts.excerpt: Drax confirms that it has signed an agreement to develop a strategic partnership with Brookfield and Radiant... Strategic partnership targeting development of >1GW data centre at Drax Power Station

key_facts.fact: Phase 1 targets up to 100MW operational from Q1 2028 on grid power; Phase 2 aims for another 500MW between 2028 and 2031, using the plant's own generation behind the meter under a long-term PPA (power purchase agreement).
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 1: targeting up to 100MW, operational from Q1 2028; Phase 2: ambition to ramp up to an additional 500MW of capacity between 2028 and 2031... behind-the-meter with around-the-clock power directly to a data centre under a long-term PPA agreement

key_facts.fact: Brookfield estimates total investment, including chips, could exceed £20 billion, with £2.5 billion in Phase 1, backed by the Brookfield-Qai AI infrastructure joint venture.
key_facts.excerpt: Brookfield estimates that total potential investment, including semiconductor chips, could exceed £20 billion, with an initial £2.5 billion as a part of Phase 1

key_facts.fact: Phase 1 still depends on planning and regulatory approvals, securing a tenant and final investment decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial phase is subject to planning, regulatory and network approvals from the government and relevant agencies, alongside securing a tenant for the project... final investment decisions are yet to be made.

key_facts.fact: Drax shares rose 8.8% in early London trading on Nov. 3.
key_facts.excerpt: London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.8% in early morning trading.

key_facts.fact: The Guardian notes the Drax plant is Britain's most polluting power station, and it could power the country's largest data center.
key_facts.excerpt: Britain's most polluting power plant could soon power the country's largest datacentre under a £20bn deal to build AI infrastructure on the site of the Drax power plant in North Yorkshire.

stories.headline: Apple's Ternus calls memory prices 'unprecedented' as inventory jumps 154% and margins guided lower

key_facts.fact: Apple CEO John Ternus said on the Nov. 2 earnings call that 'what we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented' and that Apple expects 'even higher memory costs' in the December quarter, with costs continuing to rise afterward.
key_facts.excerpt: "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," said Apple CEO John Ternus... He said that the company expected "even higher memory costs" in the December quarter... Ternus also said that beyond December, Apple expects memory costs "continuing to increase."

key_facts.fact: Apple guided a December-quarter gross margin of 45%-46%, down from 47.9% in the September quarter, largely because of higher memory costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's forecast of a 45% to 46% gross margin in the December quarter was largely attributed to the impact of higher memory costs. The company reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.

key_facts.fact: Inventory rose to $14.54 billion, up 31.1% from $11.09 billion in Q3 and 154.3% from $5.72 billion a year earlier, as Apple stockpiled memory.
key_facts.excerpt: growing from $11.09 billion in Q3 to $14.54 billion in Q4, a jump of 31.1%. Year-over-year, inventory grew 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.

key_facts.fact: Manufacturing purchase obligations rose by $33 billion from the June to the September quarter as Apple works to secure supply.
key_facts.excerpt: "As we work to improve supply, our manufacturing purchase obligations have increased by 33 billion dollars from June to the September quarter..."

key_facts.fact: Apple blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales: iPad revenue fell 10% to $6.2 billion, below the $6.7 billion analysts expected; COO Sabih Khan did not rule out further price increases.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter... iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts' expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year... did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.

sources.title: Apple's inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb
